query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the formation of a stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface, which acts as a barrier to metal-to-metal contact and reduces adhesive wear.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.intervention: controlled change in coating composition by adding 1 at.% Ti to the FeNiCrCoCu alloy
generation.conditions: high-temperature operating regime (700°C) with a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and a normal load of 10 N
generation.structural_mediator: stable, coherent oxide layer at the surface
generation.mechanism: reduction of adhesive wear through the formation of a barrier to metal-to-metal contact
generation.predicted_outcome: 30% reduction in wear rate and 25% reduction in microscopic deformation relative to the baseline coating condition
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating without Ti addition
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance and deformation behavior may be influenced by other factors such as coating thickness, substrate material, and sliding conditions, which are not considered in this hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: controlled sliding wear experiment with the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating with and without Ti addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the wear rate and microscopic deformation of the Ti-added coating are not reduced by at least 20% relative to the baseline coating condition, the hypothesis is falsified
